Q: How do executables being part of the same application find eachother on MS Windows? A:

The normal way to do this is simply to have the binaries in the same directory. The program name can be predictable, but the directory it's installed in is never predictable.

It can be found here: How do I find the location of the executable in C?

Even on Linux/Unix you never hard-code the path into the executable.

On MS Windows you can find the program directory using GetModuleFileName as described here: How to get the program path i am executing with "open with" method?

Q: Why does is.na(NULL) returns logical(0) and not FALSE? A:

If you want is.na(NULL) to return FALSE try testing its return value with isTRUE.

isTRUE(is.na(NULL))
#> [1] FALSE

Created on 2026-01-17 with reprex v2.1.1

From the documentation help("isTRUE"):

isTRUE(x) is the same as { is.logical(x) && length(x) == 1 && !is.na(x) && x }; isFALSE() is defined analogously. Consequently, if(isTRUE(cond)) may be preferable to if(cond) because of NAs.
In earlier R versions, isTRUE <- function(x) identical(x, TRUE), had the drawback to be false e.g., for x <- c(val = TRUE).

Q: Error: "PrismaConfigEnvError: Missing required environment variable: DATABASE_URL" A:

This usually happens when Prisma is trying to read the env during build time, not runtime, and DATABASE_URL just isn’t actually loaded in the process that’s running Prisma.

A couple of things that normally cause it:

  • .env isn’t in the root where Prisma expects it

  • The env file exists, but Next.js isn’t loading it, because you didn’t restart the development server

  • You’re running a command like prisma generate or prisma db push from outside the project root, so it can’t see the env file

  • Or you put DATABASE_URL in .env.local, but Prisma only loads .env by default

The easiest fix:
Make sure you have a .env in the project root with:

DATABASE_URL="mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/dbname"

Then restart your terminal or development server, so Prisma actually picks it up.

Prisma doesn’t magically load Next.js env layers; it just reads from the real env of the running process. If that variable isn’t there at command time, it throws that exact error.

Q: Unable to install ggmosaic A:

I had the same problem (Jan 2026). Fixed it with the solution given by VisruthSK here:

https://github.com/haleyjeppson/ggmosaic/issues/85

Installing ggmosaic from GitHub solved this issue for me--it seems like there was a patch which is yet to be published to CRAN.

I am on Windows and made sure to have the latest versions of R, RStudio and Rtools. Then installed from GitHub using the code in the README. ggmosaic is working for me now.

Q: Meson on windows cannot find llvm-lib? A:

Just had this same error in the question. My solution was to:

  1. Go into the Visual Studio Installer
  2. Choose "Modify" the installed Visual Studio version
  3. Go to the "Individual components" tab
  4. Select "MSVC Build Tools for x64/x86", then click "Modify"

Q: How to allocate a value of a line from a file into an array in C? A:

You don't have a complete example posted, and I don't know what your declaration of todo_list is, but...

Change this:

 while (fgets(task, MAX_CHARS, data_file))

To:

 while (fgets(todo_list [i], MAX_CHARS, data_file))

But you have other issues. What is task_counter equal to when you load the file?

Q: How do I solve my problem with compiling my .S file (GAS (GNU ASM))? A:

Error: expected an integer or zero register at operand 3 -- ``mul x0,x0,#1000000' -- you shall use a register ; Change :

mul x0,x0, #1000000

To :

ldr x1,#1000000
mul x0,x0,x1

Error: unknown pseudo-op: ``.add' -- you've added a dot, you could change to this :

add    x5,x5,0
add    x6,x6,0

Note: You're just adding 0, maybe you can just remove these lines ?

Error: immediate out of range -- you cannot sub/add using an immedate value that large ; Change :

sub x0,x0,#1000000
add x2,x2,#1000000000

To :

sub x0,x0,x1
ldr x1,#1000000000
add x2,x2,x1
